structural_memory.memory: Cargo-tank washing/cleaning service spans owner/manager, master and deck/cargo team, engineering crew, shore technical or cargo support, tank-washing/cleaning equipment or service actors and relevant terminal, port or yard support. Cleaning-function readiness, tank scope, support and monitoring should remain distinct roles rather than one tank-cleaning or operating directory.

Cleaning-machine or cleaning-function readiness is distinct from wash-medium supply/support readiness. A supply/support function can be available while the cleaning machinery or delivered cleaning function is unavailable, and machinery concern does not itself prove a supply failure.

Wash-medium supply/support confidence is distinct from exact medium composition, temperature, pressure or flow. Structural memory can represent whether supply/support is available, degraded, uncertain or restored without retaining preparation or adjustment guidance.

Cleaning distribution or path availability is distinct from cleaning-machine readiness. Machinery can be ready while the intended bounded distribution path is unavailable or uncertain, and path uncertainty does not by itself prove machinery failure.

Tank-scope or tank-interface confidence is distinct from common cleaning-system availability. A common cleaning service can be available while one tank, tank group or bounded interface remains unavailable or uncertain.

Non-numeric cleaning-function confidence can be represented as available, degraded, uncertain, restricted or restored for the intended tank scope without retaining cleanliness acceptance criteria, residue limits, wash duration, sequence or operating targets.

Return, collection or drainage-path confidence can be represented as a separate bounded service state from delivery of wash medium. Cleaning delivery may be available while the downstream collection/return path remains uncertain, without retaining valve lineups or disposal procedures.

Monitoring or indication confidence is distinct from actual cleaning-function confidence. Instrument, status or alarm information can change confidence but does not alone establish tank condition, cleaning effectiveness, root cause or required action.

Redundancy or substitution confidence can exist across cleaning machinery, supply/support paths, distribution paths or tank scopes, but structural memory should not infer exact approved lineups, nozzle patterns, capacities, cross-connections or sequences.

Tank-washing/cleaning degradation follows a defensive lifecycle: observation, uncertain machinery/supply/path/tank/collection/monitoring scope, affected-state identification, restriction or uncertainty, bounded isolation, restoration indication and post-restoration verification. No tank-cleaning, gas-freeing, entry or emergency procedure is retained.

Restriction or isolation should be scoped to the affected cleaning unit/function, supply/support path, distribution segment, collection/return path, tank scope or monitoring domain rather than generalized to the entire cargo system. Exact valve or machine actions remain deferred.

Tank-washing/cleaning degradation can propagate into cargo-change flexibility, tank-condition confidence, inspection/readiness, terminal compatibility, rework or schedule, but those downstream effects are not themselves proof of a cleaning-machine, supply, distribution, tank-interface, collection or monitoring root cause.

Restoration can have multiple timestamps: cleaning-machine/function readiness returns, supply/support and distribution confidence are re-established, affected tank scope is available, collection/return confidence is renewed, monitoring confidence returns and cleaning-function confidence is separately verified. One machine-running indication does not prove full restoration.

P092 liquid-cargo transfer concerns movement of cargo through transfer pumps and paths, while P098 concerns a distinct tank-washing/cleaning service. Transfer readiness does not equal cleaning readiness, and cleaning degradation does not prove cargo-transfer failure.

P094 tank heating and P081 generic steam/boiler service can provide heat or utility support in some cleaning contexts, but upstream heat/steam availability does not equal delivered tank-washing/cleaning function.
P071 water-service concepts can support wash-medium availability, but generic water readiness does not establish cargo-tank cleaning supply, distribution, collection or cleaning-function confidence.

P067 equipment lifecycle concepts refine cleaning-machine condition and restoration, but an equipment lifecycle state does not equal delivered tank-washing/cleaning service across the intended tank scope.
Generic machinery, support, path, tank-scope, monitoring and restoration mechanics overlap prior shipboard utility, equipment and cargo-service passes.

Scoped degradation, restriction/isolation, downstream-effect separation and multi-stage restoration mechanics overlap prior shipboard service passes; P098 applies them specifically to cargo-tank washing/cleaning.
